## One System, Two Regions

<!-- STEP id="setup" -->
Treat the whole rope as one system: total mass $M$, total length $L$.

A length $l$ hangs over the table's edge.

<!-- STEP id="on-table-cancels" -->
## The Part Still on the Table

Weight pulls it down. The table's normal force pushes it back up.

They cancel — exactly the same balance as any block resting on a table.

<!-- STEP id="hanging-drives-it" -->
## The Part Hanging Over the Edge

Nothing cancels its weight. That hanging fraction's weight is the only unbalanced force on the whole system:

$$\frac{l}{L}Mg = Ma$$

<!-- STEP id="mass-cancels" -->
## The Total Mass Cancels

$$a = \frac{l}{L}g$$

$M$ disappears completely from the answer. **A heavier rope slides off at exactly the same rate, for the same hanging fraction.**
